<h1 id="cloud-search-api">Cloud Search API v1</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Cloud Search provides cloud-based search capabilities over Google Workspace data. The Cloud Search API allows indexing of non-Google Workspace data into Cloud Search.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://cloudsearch.googleapis.com/">https://cloudsearch.googleapis.com/</a>

<a href="https://developers.google.com/terms/">Terms of service</a>
Web: <a href="https://google.com">Google</a> 
License: <a href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/">Creative Commons Attribution 3.0</a>

<a href="https://developers.google.com/cloud-search/docs/guides/">External documentation</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication. Oauth 2.0 implicit authentication

    - Flow: implicit
    - Authorization URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.debug|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.indexing|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.query|Search your organization's data in the Cloud Search index|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.settings|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.settings.indexing|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.settings.query|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.stats|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.stats.indexing|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|

- oAuth2 authentication. Oauth 2.0 authorizationCode authentication

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth)
    - Token URL = [https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token](https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.debug|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.indexing|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.query|Search your organization's data in the Cloud Search index|
|https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud_search.settings|Index and serve your organization's data with Cloud Search|

## cloudsearch.debug.datasources.items.searchByViewUrl

<a id="opIdcloudsearch.debug.datasources.items.searchByViewUrl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.googleapis.com/v1/debug/string/items:searchByViewUrl \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "debugOptions": {
      "enableDebugging": true
    },
    "pageToken": "string",
    "viewUrl": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/debug/{name}/items:searchByViewUrl`

Fetches the item whose viewUrl exactly matches that of the URL provided in the request. **Note:** This API requires an admin account to execute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "debugOptions": {
    "enableDebugging": true
  },
  "pageToken": "string",
  "viewUrl": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="cloudsearchdebugdatasourcesitemssearchbyviewurl-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Source name, format: datasources/{source_id}|

## cloudsearch.debug.datasources.items.checkAccess

<a id="opIdcloudsearch.debug.datasources.items.checkAccess"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.googleapis.com/v1/debug/string:checkAccess \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "groupResourceName": "string",
    "gsuitePrincipal": {
      "gsuiteDomain": true,
      "gsuiteGroupEmail": "string",
      "gsuiteUserEmail": "string"
    },
    "userResourceName": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/debug/{name}:checkAccess`

Checks whether an item is accessible by specified principal. Principal must be a user; groups and domain values aren't supported. **Note:** This API requires an admin account to execute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "groupResourceName": "string",
  "gsuitePrincipal": {
    "gsuiteDomain": true,
    "gsuiteGroupEmail": "string",
    "gsuiteUserEmail": "string"
  },
  "userResourceName": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="cloudsearchdebugdatasourcesitemscheckaccess-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Item name, format: datasources/{source_id}/items/{item_id}|
|debugOptions.enableDebugging|query|boolean|false|If you are asked by Google to help with debugging, set this field. Otherwise, ignore this field.|
|$.xgafv|query|string|false|V1 error format.|
|access_token|query|string|false|OAuth access token.|
|alt|query|string|false|Data format for response.|
|callback|query|string|false|JSONP|
|fields|query|string|false|Selector specifying which fields to include in a partial response.|

|oauth_token|query|string|false|OAuth 2.0 token for the current user.|
|prettyPrint|query|boolean|false|Returns response with indentations and line breaks.|

|upload_protocol|query|string|false|Upload protocol for media (e.g. "raw", "multipart").|
|uploadType|query|string|false|Legacy upload protocol for media (e.g. "media", "multipart").|
|body|body|[Principal](#schemaprincipal)|false|none|

|» userResourceName|body|string|false|This principal is a user identified using an external identity. The name field must specify the user resource name with this format: identitysources/{source_id}/users/{ID}|

## cloudsearch.indexing.datasources.items.poll

<a id="opIdcloudsearch.indexing.datasources.items.poll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.googleapis.com/v1/indexing/string/items:poll \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "connectorName": "string",
    "debugOptions": {
      "enableDebugging": true
    },
    "limit": 0,
    "queue": "string",
    "statusCodes": [
      "CODE_UNSPECIFIED"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/indexing/{name}/items:poll`

Polls for unreserved items from the indexing queue and marks a set as reserved, starting with items that have the oldest timestamp from the highest priority ItemStatus. The priority order is as follows: ERROR MODIFIED NEW_ITEM ACCEPTED Reserving items ensures that polling from other threads cannot create overlapping sets. After handling the reserved items, the client should put items back into the unreserved state, either by calling index, or by calling push with the type REQUEUE. Items automatically become available (unreserved) after 4 hours even if no update or push method is called. This API requires an admin or service account to execute. The service account used is the one whitelisted in the corresponding data source.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "connectorName": "string",
  "debugOptions": {
    "enableDebugging": true
  },
  "limit": 0,
  "queue": "string",
  "statusCodes": [
    "CODE_UNSPECIFIED"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="cloudsearchindexingdatasourcesitemspoll-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|The name of the Data Source to poll items. Format: datasources/{source_id}|
|$.xgafv|query|string|false|V1 error format.|
|access_token|query|string|false|OAuth access token.|
|alt|query|string|false|Data format for response.|

|body|body|[PollItemsRequest](#schemapollitemsrequest)|false|none|
|» connectorName|body|string|false|The name of connector making this call. Format: datasources/{source_id}/connectors/{ID}|

`POST /v1/indexing/{name}/items:unreserve`

## cloudsearch.media.upload

<a id="opIdcloudsearch.media.upload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.googleapis.com/v1/media/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"resourceName":"string"}'
```

`POST /v1/media/{resourceName}`

Uploads media for indexing. The upload endpoint supports direct and resumable upload protocols and is intended for large items that can not be [inlined during index requests](https://developers.google.com/cloud-search/docs/reference/rest/v1/indexing.datasources.items#itemcontent). To index large content: 1. Call indexing.datasources.items.upload with the item name to begin an upload session and retrieve the UploadItemRef. 1. Call media.upload to upload the content, as a streaming request, using the same resource name from the UploadItemRef from step 1. 1. Call indexing.datasources.items.index to index the item. Populate the [ItemContent](/cloud-search/docs/reference/rest/v1/indexing.datasources.items#ItemContent) with the UploadItemRef from step 1. For additional information, see [Create a content connector using the REST API](https://developers.google.com/cloud-search/docs/guides/content-connector#rest). **Note:** This API requires a service account to execute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resourceName": "string"
}
```

`POST /v1/query/search`

The Cloud Search Query API provides the search method, which returns the most relevant results from a user query. The results can come from Google Workspace apps, such as Gmail or Google Drive, or they can come from data that you have indexed from a third party. **Note:** This API requires a standard end user account to execute. A service account can't perform Query API requests directly; to use a service account to perform queries, set up [Google Workspace domain-wide delegation of authority](https://developers.google.com/cloud-search/docs/guides/delegation/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contextAttributes": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "values": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "dataSourceRestrictions": [
    {
      "filterOptions": [
        {
          "filter": {
            "compositeFilter": {},
            "valueFilter": {
              "operatorName": "string",
              "value": {
                "booleanValue": true,
                "dateValue": {
                  "day": 0,
                  "month": 0,
                  "year": 0
                },
                "doubleValue": 0,
```

`GET /v1/query/sources`

A service account can't perform Query API requests directly; to use a service account to perform queries, set up [Google Workspace domain-wide delegation of authority](https://developers.google.com/cloud-search/docs/guides/delegation/).

## cloudsearch.stats.getIndex

<a id="opIdcloudsearch.stats.getIndex"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.googleapis.com/v1/stats/index \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/stats/index`

Gets indexed item statistics aggreggated across all data sources. This API only returns statistics for previous dates; it doesn't return statistics for the current day. **Note:** This API requires a standard end user account to execute.

<h3 id="cloudsearchstatsgetindex-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|fromDate.year|query|integer|false|Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999.|
|toDate.day|query|integer|false|Day of month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month.|
|toDate.month|query|integer|false|Month of date. Must be from 1 to 12.|
|toDate.year|query|integer|false|Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999.|

Get the users statistics for search application. **Note:** This API requires a standard end user account to execute.

<h3 id="cloudsearchstatsusersearchapplicationsget-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|fromDate.month|query|integer|false|Month of date. Must be from 1 to 12.|
|fromDate.year|query|integer|false|Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999.|
|toDate.day|query|integer|false|Day of month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month.|
|toDate.month|query|integer|false|Month of date. Must be from 1 to 12.|
|toDate.year|query|integer|false|Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999.|

```json
    "string"
  ],

  "shouldFix": true
}
```

The request set by clients to instruct Backend how the user intend to fix the ACL. Technically it's not a request to ACL Fixer, because Backend uses /DriveService.Share to modify Drive ACLs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|recipientEmails|[string]|false|none|For Spaces messages: This field is ignored. For DMs messages: The list of email addresses that should be added to the Drive item's ACL. In general, the list should not be empty when the boolean "should_fix" field is set; otherwise, the list should be empty. During transition - when clients do not specify this field but the "should_fix" is true, we follow the legacy behavior: share to all users in the DM regardless of emails. This behavior is being phased out.|
|role|string|false|none|none|
|shouldFix|boolean|false|none|Whether to attempt to fix the ACL by adding the room or DM members to the Drive file's ACL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|UNKNOWN|
|role|READER|
|role|COMMENTER|
|role|WRITER|

|fixableEmailAddress|[string]|false|none|List of recipient email addresses for which access can be granted. This field contains the same email addresses from the GetMessagePreviewMetadata request if all recipients can be successfully added to the ACL as determined by Drive ACL Fixer. For now, the field is non-empty if and only if the "fixability" value is "CAN_FIX".|
|outOfDomainWarningEmailAddress|[string]|false|none|List of recipient email addresses for which an out-of-domain-sharing warning must be shown, stating that these email addresses are not in the Google Apps organization that the requested item belong to. Empty if all recipients are in the same Google Apps organization.|

|fixability|ALREADY_ACCESSIBLE|
|fixability|CAN_FIX|

<h2 id="tocS_AffectedMembership">AffectedMembership</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaffectedmembership"></a>
<a id="schema_AffectedMembership"></a>
<a id="tocSaffectedmembership"></a>
<a id="tocsaffectedmembership"></a>

```json
{
  "affectedMember": {
    "rosterId": {
      "id": "string"
    },
    "userId": {
      "actingUserId": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "originAppId": {
        "appType": "APP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
        "gsuiteAppType": "GSUITE_APP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
        "id": "string"
      },
      "type": "HUMAN"
    }
  },
  "priorMembershipRole": "ROLE_UNKNOWN",
  "priorMembershipState": "MEMBER_UNKNOWN",
  "targetMembershipRole": "ROLE_UNKNOWN"
}
```

Earlier we used to populate just the affected_members list and inferred the new membership state (roles didn't exist back then) from the Type. go/dynamite-finra required backend to know the previous membership state to reconstruct membership history. The proper solution involved cleaning up up Type enum, but it was used in many, many places. This was added as a stop-gap solution to unblock FINRA without breaking everything. Later role update and target audience update started relying on this to communicate information to clients about what transition happened. So this is now required to be populated and should be in sync with affected_members for new messages.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|affectedMember|[MemberId](#schemamemberid)|false|none|Eventually this can be updated to a oneOf User, Space (for nested spaces), Bots or Service, as and when these use cases come up.|
|priorMembershipRole|string|false|none|none|
|priorMembershipState|string|false|none|none|
|targetMembershipRole|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|priorMembershipRole|ROLE_UNKNOWN|
|priorMembershipRole|ROLE_NONE|
|priorMembershipRole|ROLE_INVITEE|
|priorMembershipRole|ROLE_MEMBER|
|priorMembershipRole|ROLE_OWNER|
|priorMembershipState|MEMBER_UNKNOWN|
|priorMembershipState|MEMBER_INVITED|

<h2 id="tocS_AllAuthenticatedUsersProto">AllAuthenticatedUsersProto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaallauthenticatedusersproto"></a>
<a id="schema_AllAuthenticatedUsersProto"></a>
<a id="tocSallauthenticatedusersproto"></a>
<a id="tocsallauthenticatedusersproto"></a>

```json
{}
```

Represents a principal who has authenticated as any kind of user which the application understands. This is typically used for "wiki-like" security, where anyone is allowed access so long as they can be held accountable for that access. Since the purpose is knowing whom to blame, it is up to the application to decide what kinds of users it knows how to blame. For example, an application might choose to include GAIA users in "all authenticated users", but not include MDB users. Nothing here.

Metadata used only in Dynamite backend for uploaded attachments.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|blobPath|string|false|none|Blobstore path for the uploaded attachment|
|contentName|string|false|none|The original file name for the content, not the full path.|
|contentSize|string(int64)|false|none|Scotty reported content size by default. http://google3/uploader/agent/scotty_agent.proto?l=101&rcl=140889785|
|contentType|string|false|none|Type is from Scotty's best_guess by default: http://google3/uploader/agent/scotty_agent.proto?l=51&rcl=140889785|
|dlpScanOutcome|string|false|none|The results of the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) scan of the attachment. DEPRECATED: use dlp_scan_summary instead.|
|dlpScanSummary|[DlpScanSummary](#schemadlpscansummary)|false|none|Summary of a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) scan of the attachment. Attachments are evaluated in the backend when they are uploaded.|
|groupId|[GroupId](#schemagroupid)|false|none|GroupId to which this attachment is uploaded.|
|isClientSideTranscodedVideo|boolean|false|none|If the uploaded file is a video that has been transcoded on the client side Next tag: 18|
|originalDimension|[AppsDynamiteSharedDimension](#schemaappsdynamiteshareddimension)|false|none|Original dimension of the content. Only set for image attachments.|
|quoteReplyMessageId|[MessageId](#schemamessageid)|false|none|The message id of a quote reply referencing this attachment. When present, this attachment has been quoted in a reply message. Normally, the attachment is fetched through the message id in the blob_path, but in the case of a quote reply, the blob_path would contain the quoted message id. Thus this message id field is needed to fetch the quote reply message instead. This field is conditionally populated at read time for quotes and never persisted in storage. See go/message-quoting-attachments for more context.|
|sha256|string(byte)|false|none|The SHA256 hash of the attachment bytes.|
|uploadIp|string|false|none|User IP address at upload time. Ex. "123.1.2.3". Used by Ares abuse scanning.|
|uploadTimestampUsec|string(int64)|false|none|Timestamp of when user finished uploading the content.|
|videoId|string|false|none|VideoID of the video attachments. This ID shall meets the Youtube ID format of 16 hex characters. For example, '4c14b8825af6059b' is a valid ID.|
|videoThumbnailBlobId|string|false|none|Full Blobstore ID for the video thumbnail.|
|virusScanResult|string|false|none|Result for a virus scan.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_FAILURE_TIMEOUT|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_FAILURE_ALL_RULES_FAILED|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_FAILURE_ILLEGAL_STATE_FOR_ATTACHMENTS|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_SKIPPED_EXPERIMENT_DISABLED|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_SKIPPED_CONSUMER|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_SKIPPED_NON_HUMAN_USER|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_SKIPPED_NO_MESSAGE|
|dlpScanOutcome|SCAN_SKIPPED_USER_ACKNOWLEDGED_WARNING|

```json
{
  "blobId": "string",
  "contentType": "string",
  "createTimeMicros": "string",
  "creatorUserId": {
    "actingUserId": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "originAppId": {
      "appType": "APP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
      "gsuiteAppType": "GSUITE_APP_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
      "id": "string"
    },
    "type": "HUMAN"
  },
  "deleteTimeMicros": "string",
  "ephemeralUrl": "string",
  "ownerCustomerId": {
    "customerId": "string"
  },
  "readToken": "string",
  "shortcode": "string",
  "state": "EMOJI_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "updateTimeMicros": "string",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

Proto representation of a custom emoji. May be used in both APIs and in Spanner, but certain fields should be restricted to one or the other. See the per-field documentation for details. NEXT_TAG: 14

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|blobId|string|false|none|ID for the underlying image data in Blobstore. This field should *only* be present in Spanner or within the server, but should not be exposed in public APIs.|
|contentType|string|false|none|Content type of the file used to upload the emoji. Used for takeout. Written to Spanner when the emoji is created.|
|createTimeMicros|string(int64)|false|none|Time when the Emoji was created, in microseconds. This field may be present in Spanner, within the server, or in public APIs.|
|creatorUserId|[UserId](#schemauserid)|false|none|This field should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|deleteTimeMicros|string(int64)|false|none|Time when the emoji was deleted, in microseconds. This field may be present in Spanner, within the server, or in public APIs. Only present if the emoji has been deleted.|
|ephemeralUrl|string|false|read-only|Output only. A short-lived URL clients can use for directly accessing a custom emoji image. This field is intended for API consumption, and should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|ownerCustomerId|[CustomerId](#schemacustomerid)|false|none|This field should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|readToken|string|false|none|Opaque token that clients use to construct the URL for accessing the custom emoji’s image data. This field is intended for API consumption, and should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|shortcode|string|false|none|User-provided, human-readable ID for the custom emoji. Users are expected to observe this field in the UI instead of the UUID. This shortcode should be unique within an organization, but has no global uniqueness guarantees, unlike the UUID. This field should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|state|string|false|none|Snapshot of the current state of the emoji, which may differ from the source-of-truth in the CustomEmojis table. This field should *never* be persisted to Spanner.|
|updateTimeMicros|string(int64)|false|none|none|
|uuid|string|false|none|Unique key for a custom emoji resource. Required. This field is *always* populated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|EMOJI_STATE_UNSPECIFIED|
|state|EMOJI_ENABLED|
|state|EMOJI_SYSTEM_DISABLED|
|state|EMOJI_HIDDEN|
|state|EMOJI_DELETED|

<h2 id="tocS_AppsDynamiteStorageAction">AppsDynamiteStorageAction</h2>

```json
{

  "interaction": "INTERACTION_UNSPECIFIED",
  "loadIndicator": "SPINNER",
  "parameters": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "persistValues": true
}
```

An action that describes the behavior when the form is submitted. For example, an Apps Script can be invoked to handle the form.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|function|string|false|none|Apps Script function to invoke when the containing element is clicked/activated.|
|interaction|string|false|none|none|
|loadIndicator|string|false|none|none|
|parameters|[[AppsDynamiteStorageActionActionParameter](#schemaappsdynamitestorageactionactionparameter)]|false|none|List of action parameters.|
|persistValues|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether form values persist after the action. The default value is `false`. If `true`, form values remain after the action is triggered. When using [LoadIndicator.NONE](workspace/add-ons/reference/rpc/google.apps.card.v1#loadindicator) for actions, `persist_values` = `true`is recommended, as it ensures that any changes made by the user after form or on change actions are sent to the server are not overwritten by the response. If `false`, the form values are cleared when the action is triggered. When `persist_values` is set to `false`, it is strongly recommended that the card use [LoadIndicator.SPINNER](workspace/add-ons/reference/rpc/google.apps.card.v1#loadindicator) for all actions, as this locks the UI to ensure no changes are made by the user while the action is being processed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|interaction|INTERACTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|interaction|OPEN_DIALOG|
|loadIndicator|SPINNER|
|loadIndicator|NONE|

Represents the complete border style applied to widgets.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cornerRadius|integer(int32)|false|none|The corner radius for the border.|
|strokeColor|[Color](#schemacolor)|false|none|The colors to use when the type is `BORDER_TYPE_STROKE`.|
|type|string|false|none|The border type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|BORDER_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|type|NO_BORDER|
|type|STROKE|

|disabled|boolean|false|none|If true, the button is displayed in a disabled state and doesn't respond to user actions.|
|icon|[AppsDynamiteStorageIcon](#schemaappsdynamitestorageicon)|false|none|The icon image.|
|onClick|[AppsDynamiteStorageOnClick](#schemaappsdynamitestorageonclick)|false|none|The action to perform when the button is clicked.|
|text|string|false|none|The text of the button.|

A card is a UI element that can contain UI widgets such as text and images. For more information, see Cards . For example, the following JSON creates a card that has a header with the name, position, icons, and link for a contact, followed by a section with contact information like email and phone number. ``` { "header": { "title": "Heba Salam", "subtitle": "Software Engineer", "imageStyle": "ImageStyle.AVATAR", "imageUrl": "https://example.com/heba_salam.png", "imageAltText": "Avatar for Heba Salam" }, "sections" : [ { "header": "Contact Info", "widgets": [ { "decorated_text": { "icon": { "knownIcon": "EMAIL" }, "content": "heba.salam@example.com" } }, { "decoratedText": { "icon": { "knownIcon": "PERSON" }, "content": "Online" } }, { "decoratedText": { "icon": { "knownIcon": "PHONE" }, "content": "+1 (555) 555-1234" } }, { "buttons": [ { "textButton": { "text": "Share", }, "onClick": { "openLink": { "url": "https://example.com/share" } } }, { "textButton": { "text": "Edit", }, "onClick": { "action": { "function": "goToView", "parameters": [ { "key": "viewType", "value": "EDIT" } ], "loadIndicator": "LoadIndicator.SPINNER" } } } ] } ], "collapsible": true, "uncollapsibleWidgetsCount": 3 } ], "cardActions": [ { "actionLabel": "Send Feedback", "onClick": { "openLink": { "url": "https://example.com/feedback" } } } ], "name": "contact-card-K3wB6arF2H9L" } ```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cardActions|[[AppsDynamiteStorageCardCardAction](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecardcardaction)]|false|none|The actions of this card. They are added to a card's generated toolbar menu. For example, the following JSON constructs a card action menu with Settings and Send Feedback options: ``` "card_actions": [ { "actionLabel": "Setting", "onClick": { "action": { "functionName": "goToView", "parameters": [ { "key": "viewType", "value": "SETTING" } ], "loadIndicator": "LoadIndicator.SPINNER" } } }, { "actionLabel": "Send Feedback", "onClick": { "openLink": { "url": "https://example.com/feedback" } } } ] ```|
|header|[AppsDynamiteStorageCardCardHeader](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecardcardheader)|false|none|The header of the card. A header usually contains a title and an image.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the card, which is used as a identifier for the card in card navigation.|
|sections|[[AppsDynamiteStorageCardSection](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecardsection)]|false|none|Sections are separated by a line divider.|

A card action is the action associated with the card. For example, an invoice card might include actions such as delete invoice, email invoice, or open the invoice in a browser.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actionLabel|string|false|none|The label that displays as the action menu item.|
|onClick|[AppsDynamiteStorageOnClick](#schemaappsdynamitestorageonclick)|false|none|The onclick action for this action item.|

```json
{
  "imageAltText": "string",
  "imageType": "SQUARE",
  "imageUrl": "string",
  "subtitle": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|imageAltText|string|false|none|The alternative text of this image which is used for accessibility.|
|imageType|string|false|none|The image's type.|
|imageUrl|string|false|none|The URL of the image in the card header.|
|subtitle|string|false|none|The subtitle of the card header.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the card header. The title must be specified. The header has a fixed height: if both a title and subtitle are specified, each takes up one line. If only the title is specified, it takes up both lines.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|imageType|SQUARE|
|imageType|CIRCLE|


A section contains a collection of widgets that are rendered vertically in the order that they are specified. Across all platforms, cards have a narrow fixed width, so there is currently no need for layout properties, for example, float.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collapsible|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this section is collapsible. If a section is collapsible, the description must be given.|
|header|string|false|none|The header of the section. Formatted text is supported.|
|uncollapsibleWidgetsCount|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of uncollapsible widgets. For example, when a section contains five widgets and the `numUncollapsibleWidget` is set to `2`, the first two widgets are always shown and the last three are collapsed as default. The `numUncollapsibleWidget` is taken into account only when collapsible is set to `true`.|
|widgets|[[AppsDynamiteStorageWidget](#schemaappsdynamitestoragewidget)]|false|none|A section must contain at least 1 widget.|


Represents a Columns widget that displays a single row of columns.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|columnItems|[[AppsDynamiteStorageColumnsColumn](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecolumnscolumn)]|false|none|Each card supports up to 2 columns.|
|wrapStyle|string|false|none|Controls how the column resizes based on screen width.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|wrapStyle|WRAP_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED|
|wrapStyle|NOWRAP|
|wrapStyle|WRAP|


Represents a Column that consists of widgets stacked vertically.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|horizontalAlignment|string|false|none|The horizontal alignment of the column.|
|horizontalSizeStyle|string|false|none|Specifies how the column content is sized horizontally.|
|verticalAlignment|string|false|none|The vertical alignment of the column.|
|widgets|[[AppsDynamiteStorageColumnsColumnWidgets](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecolumnscolumnwidgets)]|false|none|LINT.ThenChange(//depot/google3/google/apps/card/v1/card.proto) Array of widgets included in the column.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|horizontalAlignment|HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_UNSPECIFIED|
|horizontalAlignment|START|
|horizontalAlignment|CENTER|
|horizontalAlignment|END|
|horizontalSizeStyle|HORIZONTAL_SIZE_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED|
|horizontalSizeStyle|FILL_AVAILABLE_SPACE|
|horizontalSizeStyle|FILL_MINIMUM_SPACE|
|verticalAlignment|VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_UNSPECIFIED|
|verticalAlignment|CENTER|
|verticalAlignment|TOP|
|verticalAlignment|BOTTOM|

<h2 id="tocS_AppsDynamiteStorageDateTimePicker">AppsDynamiteStorageDateTimePicker</h2>


The widget that lets users to specify a date and time.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|label|string|false|none|The label for the field that displays to the user.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the text input that's used in formInput, and uniquely identifies this input.|
|onChangeAction|[AppsDynamiteStorageAction](#schemaappsdynamitestorageaction)|false|none|Triggered when the user clicks Save or Clear from the date/time picker dialog. This is only triggered if the value changed as a result of the Save/Clear operation.|
|timezoneOffsetDate|integer(int32)|false|none|The number representing the time zone offset from UTC, in minutes. If set, the `value_ms_epoch` is displayed in the specified time zone. If not set, it uses the user's time zone setting on the client side.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the date/time picker.|
|valueMsEpoch|string(int64)|false|none|The value to display as the default value before user input or previous user input. It is represented in milliseconds (Epoch time). For `DATE_AND_TIME` type, the full epoch value is used. For `DATE_ONLY` type, only date of the epoch time is used. For `TIME_ONLY` type, only time of the epoch time is used. For example, you can set epoch time to `3 * 60 * 60 * 1000` to represent 3am.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|DATE_AND_TIME|
|type|DATE_ONLY|
|type|TIME_ONLY|

A widget that displays text with optional decorations such as a label above or below the text, an icon in front of the text, a selection widget or a button after the text.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bottomLabel|string|false|none|The formatted text label that shows below the main text.|
|button|[AppsDynamiteStorageButton](#schemaappsdynamitestoragebutton)|false|none|A button that can be clicked to trigger an action.|
|endIcon|[AppsDynamiteStorageIcon](#schemaappsdynamitestorageicon)|false|none|An icon displayed after the text.|
|icon|[AppsDynamiteStorageIcon](#schemaappsdynamitestorageicon)|false|none|Deprecated in favor of start_icon.|
|onClick|[AppsDynamiteStorageOnClick](#schemaappsdynamitestorageonclick)|false|none|Only the top and bottom label and content region are clickable.|
|startIcon|[AppsDynamiteStorageIcon](#schemaappsdynamitestorageicon)|false|none|The icon displayed in front of the text.|
|switchControl|[AppsDynamiteStorageDecoratedTextSwitchControl](#schemaappsdynamitestoragedecoratedtextswitchcontrol)|false|none|A switch widget can be clicked to change its state or trigger an action.|
|text|string|false|none|Required. The main widget formatted text. See Text formatting for details.|
|topLabel|string|false|none|The formatted text label that shows above the main text.|
|wrapText|boolean|false|none|The wrap text setting. If `true`, the text is wrapped and displayed in multiline. Otherwise, the text is truncated.|

```json
{
  "fill": true,
  "grade": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "weight": 0
}
```

A [Google Font Icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons), which includes over 2500+ options. For example, to display a [check box icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons?selected=Material%20Symbols%20Outlined%3Acheck_box%3AFILL%400%3Bwght%40400%3BGRAD%400%3Bopsz%4048) with customized weight and grade, write { "name": "check_box", "fill": true, "weight": 300, "grade": -25 }

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fill|boolean|false|none|Whether it renders a filled icon. Default value is false. See Customization in [Google Font Icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons) for details.|
|grade|integer(int32)|false|none|Weight and grade affect a symbol’s thickness. Adjustments to grade are more granular than adjustments to weight and have a small impact on the size of the symbol. Choose from {-25, 0, 200}. If absent, default value is 0. If any other value is specified, a broken image icon will be displayed. See Customization in [Google Font Icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons) for details.|
|name|string|false|none|The icon name defined in the [Google Material Icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons) in snake_case. e.g. "check_box". Any invalid name will be trimmed as empty string result in the icon falied to render.|
|weight|integer(int32)|false|none|The stroke weight of the icon. Choose from {100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700}. If absent, default value is 400. If any other value is specified, a broken image icon will be displayed. See Customization in [Google Font Icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons) for details.|

```json
  "openAs": "FULL_SIZE",
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|appUri|[AppsDynamiteStorageOpenLinkAppUri](#schemaappsdynamitestorageopenlinkappuri)|false|none|Represents the platform specific uri/intent to open on each client. For example: A companion_url will open in a companion window on the web. An iOS URL and android intent will open in the corresponding hosting apps. If these platform specific URLs can't be handled correctly, i.e. if the companion isn't supported on web and the hosting apps aren't available on the mobile platforms then the `uri` will open in a new browser window on all the platforms.|
|onClose|string|false|none|none|
|openAs|string|false|none|none|
|url|string|false|none|The URL to open.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|onClose|NOTHING|
|onClose|RELOAD|
|openAs|FULL_SIZE|
|openAs|OVERLAY|

A text input is a UI item where users can input text. A text input can also have an onChange action and suggestions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoCompleteAction|[AppsDynamiteStorageAction](#schemaappsdynamitestorageaction)|false|none|The refresh function that returns suggestions based on the user's input text. If the callback is not specified, autocomplete is done in client side based on the initial suggestion items.|
|hintText|string|false|none|The hint text.|
|initialSuggestions|[AppsDynamiteStorageSuggestions](#schemaappsdynamitestoragesuggestions)|false|none|The initial suggestions made before any user input.|
|label|string|false|none|At least one of label and hintText must be specified.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the text input which is used in formInput.|
|onChangeAction|[AppsDynamiteStorageAction](#schemaappsdynamitestorageaction)|false|none|The onChange action, for example, invoke a function.|
|type|string|false|none|The style of the text, for example, a single line or multiple lines.|
|value|string|false|none|The default value when there is no input from the user.|

|type|MULTIPLE_LINE|

A widget is a UI element that presents texts, images, etc.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buttonList|[AppsDynamiteStorageButtonList](#schemaappsdynamitestoragebuttonlist)|false|none|A list of buttons. For example, the following JSON creates two buttons. The first is a filled text button and the second is an image button that opens a link: ``` "buttonList": { "buttons": [ "button": { "text": "Edit", "Color": { "Red": 255 "Green": 255 "Blue": 255 } "disabled": true }, "button": { "icon": { "knownIcon": "INVITE" "altText": "check calendar" }, "onClick": { "openLink": { "url": "https://example.com/calendar" } } }, ] } ```|
|columns|[AppsDynamiteStorageColumns](#schemaappsdynamitestoragecolumns)|false|none|Displays a single row of columns with widgets stacked vertically in each column. For example, the following JSON creates a 2 column widget each containing a single item. ``` "columns": { "wrapStyle": "WRAP", "columnItems": [ { "horizontalSizeStyle": "FILL_AVAILABLE_SPACE", "horizontalAlignment": "CENTER", "verticalAlignment" : "CENTER", "widgets": [ { "textParagraph": { "text": "First column text paragraph", } } ] }, { "horizontalSizeStyle": "FILL_AVAILABLE_SPACE", "horizontalAlignment": "CENTER", "verticalAlignment" : "CENTER", "widgets": [ { "textParagraph": { "text": "Second column text paragraph", } } ] }, ] } } ```|
|dateTimePicker|[AppsDynamiteStorageDateTimePicker](#schemaappsdynamitestoragedatetimepicker)|false|none|Displays a selection/input widget for date/time. For example, the following JSON creates a date/time picker for an appointment time: ``` "date_time_picker": { "name": "appointment_time", "label": "Book your appointment at:", "type": "DateTimePickerType.DATE_AND_TIME", "valueMsEpoch": "796435200000" } ```|
|decoratedText|[AppsDynamiteStorageDecoratedText](#schemaappsdynamitestoragedecoratedtext)|false|none|Displays a decorated text item in this widget. For example, the following JSON creates a decorated text widget showing email address: ``` "decoratedText": { "icon": { "knownIcon": "EMAIL" }, "topLabel": "Email Address", "content": "heba.salam@example.com", "bottomLabel": "This is a new Email address!", "switchWidget": { "name": "has_send_welcome_email_to_heba_salam", "selected": false, "controlType": "ControlType.CHECKBOX" } } ```|
|divider|[AppsDynamiteStorageDivider](#schemaappsdynamitestoragedivider)|false|none|Displays a divider. For example, the following JSON creates a divider: ``` "divider": { } ```|
|grid|[AppsDynamiteStorageGrid](#schemaappsdynamitestoragegrid)|false|none|Displays a grid with a collection of items. For example, the following JSON creates a 2 column grid with a single item: ``` "grid": { "title": "A fine collection of items", "numColumns": 2, "borderStyle": { "type": "STROKE", "cornerRadius": 4.0 }, "items": [ "image": { "imageUri": "https://www.example.com/image.png", "cropStyle": { "type": "SQUARE" }, "borderStyle": { "type": "STROKE" } }, "title": "An item", "textAlignment": "CENTER" ], "onClick": { "openLink": { "url":"https://www.example.com" } } } ```|
|horizontalAlignment|string|false|none|The horizontal alignment of this widget.|
|image|[AppsDynamiteStorageImage](#schemaappsdynamitestorageimage)|false|none|Displays an image in this widget. For example, the following JSON creates an image with alternative text: ``` "image": { "imageUrl": "https://example.com/heba_salam.png" "altText": "Avatar for Heba Salam" } ```|
|selectionInput|[AppsDynamiteStorageSelectionInput](#schemaappsdynamitestorageselectioninput)|false|none|Displays a switch control in this widget. For example, the following JSON creates a dropdown selection for size: ``` "switchControl": { "name": "size", "label": "Size" "type": "SelectionType.DROPDOWN", "items": [ { "text": "S", "value": "small", "selected": false }, { "text": "M", "value": "medium", "selected": true }, { "text": "L", "value": "large", "selected": false }, { "text": "XL", "value": "extra_large", "selected": false } ] } ```|
|textInput|[AppsDynamiteStorageTextInput](#schemaappsdynamitestoragetextinput)|false|none|Displays a text input in this widget. For example, the following JSON creates a text input for mail address: ``` "textInput": { "name": "mailing_address", "label": "Mailing Address" } ``` As another example, the following JSON creates a text input for programming language with static suggestions: ``` "textInput": { "name": "preferred_programing_language", "label": "Preferred Language", "initialSuggestions": { "items": [ { "text": "C++" }, { "text": "Java" }, { "text": "JavaScript" }, { "text": "Python" } ] } } ```|
|textParagraph|[AppsDynamiteStorageTextParagraph](#schemaappsdynamitestoragetextparagraph)|false|none|Displays a text paragraph in this widget. For example, the following JSON creates a bolded text: ``` "textParagraph": { "text": " *bold text*" } ```|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|horizontalAlignment|HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_UNSPECIFIED|
|horizontalAlignment|START|
|horizontalAlignment|CENTER|
|horizontalAlignment|END|

Richly formatted attachments. Documentation: - https://api.slack.com/docs/message-attachments

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actions|[[AppsDynamiteV1ApiCompatV1Action](#schemaappsdynamitev1apicompatv1action)]|false|none|Array of actions (currently only buttons).|
|attachment_type|string|false|none|Undocumented - used in interactive button examples. The only valid value appears to be "default".|
|author_icon|string|false|none|Avatar URL for the user.|
|author_link|string|false|none|URL that the user name should link to.|
|author_name|string|false|none|User name to display as the author of the message.|
|callback_id|string|false|none|Unique identifier for the collection of buttons within this attachment. Will be sent back to the action handler URL when a button is clicked.|
|color|string|false|none|A color "bar" to display to the left of the attachment.|
|fallback|string|false|none|Fallback plain-text string for clients that don't support attachments.|
|fields|[[AppsDynamiteV1ApiCompatV1Field](#schemaappsdynamitev1apicompatv1field)]|false|none|Columns of text inside the attachment body.|
|footer|string|false|none|A string displayed at the bottom of the attachment.|
|footer_icon|string|false|none|Avatar URL displayed to the left of the footer.|
|image_url|string|false|none|URL of an image to display in an image chip.|
|mrkdwn_in|[string]|false|none|List of fields to apply formatting to.|
|pretext|string|false|none|A string to show above the attachment.|
|text|string|false|none|Main text.|
|thumb_url|string|false|none|URL of a thumbnail image to display to the right of the attachment body.|
|title|string|false|none|Title string of this attachment.|
|title_link|string|false|none|URL that the title string should link to.|
|ts|integer(int32)|false|none|UNIX timestamp of the attachment.|

Markup that defines conference data associated to a Google Calendar event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conferenceId|string|false|none|Unique identifier for this conference data. Maximum 512 characters long.|
|conferenceSolutionId|string|false|none|An identifier of the conferencing solution. Must match a value from the deployment's `calendar.conferenceSolution.id` field.|
|entryPoints|[[AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupEntryPointMarkup](#schemaappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkupentrypointmarkup)]|false|none|Entry points to the conference. Maximum 300 entry points are allowed.|
|error|[AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupError](#schemaappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkuperror)|false|none|If set, it means an error occurred during conference creation.|
|note|string|false|none|Additional notes (such as instructions from the administrator, legal notices) to display to the user. Can contain HTML. Max length 2048 characters.|
|parameters|[[AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupParameter](#schemaappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkupparameter)]|false|none|Additional add-on parameters. Maximum 300 parameters are allowed.|

A way to join the conference.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessCode|string|false|none|An access code for accessing the conference. Maximum 128 characters long.|
|features|[string]|false|none|Features of the entry point, such as being toll or toll-free. One entry point can have multiple features.|
|label|string|false|none|The label of the entry point to display to the user. Maximum 512 characters long.|
|meetingCode|string|false|none|A meeting code for accessing the conference. Maximum 128 characters long.|
|passcode|string|false|none|A passcode for accessing the conference. Maximum 128 characters long.|
|password|string|false|none|A password for accessing the conference. Maximum 128 characters long.|
|pin|string|false|none|A PIN for accessing the conference. Maximum 128 characters long.|
|regionCode|string|false|none|The CLDR/ISO 3166 region code for the country associated with this entry point. Applicable only to `Type.PHONE`.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the entry point. Required.|
|uri|string|false|none|A URI for joining the conference. Supports tel: and http(s): and should be at most 1300 characters long. Required.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|features|UNKNOWN_FEATURE|
|features|TOLL|
|features|TOLL_FREE|
|type|UNKNOWN|
|type|VIDEO|
|type|PHONE|
|type|MORE|
|type|SIP|

<h2 id="tocS_AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupError">AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupError</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkuperror"></a>
<a id="schema_AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupError"></a>
<a id="tocSappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkuperror"></a>
<a id="tocsappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkuperror"></a>

```json
{
  "authenticationUrl": "string",
  "type": "UNKNOWN"
}
```

Represents an error that occurred during conference creation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticationUrl|string|false|none|If the error type is `AUTHENTICATION`, the add-on can provide a URL allowing users to log in. Maximum 1300 characters long.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of error. Required.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|UNKNOWN|
|type|AUTHENTICATION|
|type|TEMPORARY|
|type|PERMANENT|
|type|PERMISSION_DENIED|
|type|CONFERENCE_SOLUTION_FORBIDDEN|

<h2 id="tocS_AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupParameter">AppsExtensionsMarkupCalendarClientActionMarkupConferenceDataMarkupParameter</h2>

<a id="tocSappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkupparameter"></a>
<a id="tocsappsextensionsmarkupcalendarclientactionmarkupconferencedatamarkupparameter"></a>

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "value": "string"
}
```

Solution-specific parameters that are persisted with the event data and, if an update or delete is needed, are passed to the add-on. For example: `[{key: 'sessionKey', value: '123'}, {key: 'meetingId', value: '456'}]`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|false|none|The key of the parameter. Maximum 50 characters long. Required.|
|value|string|false|none|The value of the parameter. Maximum 1024 characters long. Required.|

Represents the settings for Cloud audit logging

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|logAdminReadActions|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether audit logging is on/off for admin activity read APIs i.e. Get/List DataSources, Get/List SearchApplications etc.|
|logDataReadActions|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether audit logging is on/off for data access read APIs i.e. ListItems, GetItem etc.|
|logDataWriteActions|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether audit logging is on/off for data access write APIs i.e. IndexItem etc.|
|project|string|false|none|The resource name of the GCP Project to store audit logs. Cloud audit logging will be enabled after project_name has been updated through CustomerService. Format: projects/{project_id}|

```json
  "id": "string",
  "resourceKey": "string"
}
```

A combination of an identifier for a Drive resource (e.g. file, folder, or drive) and any secrets needed to access it. The secrets should never be logged, and this proto annotates those secret fields to ensure that they are not. Clients are encouraged to use this proto rather than defining their own, to ensure that secrets are correctly annotated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|Serialized ID of the Drive resource|
|resourceKey|string|false|none|Resource key of the Drive item. This field should be unset if, depending on the context, the item does not have a resource key, or if none was specified. This must never be logged.|

|deliveryMedium|[DeliveryMedium](#schemadeliverymedium)|false|none|Stores the delivery source of messages (such as phone number for SMS).|
|eventId|string|false|none|Primary identifier used by Hangouts Classic for its events (messages).|
|messageContent|[ChatConserverMessageContent](#schemachatconservermessagecontent)|false|none|Stores message segments (text content) and attachments (media URLs).|
|wasUpdatedByBackfill|boolean|false|none|Whether or not these message properties were backfilled by go/dinnertrain.|

<h2 id="tocS_BooleanOperatorOptions">BooleanOperatorOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabooleanoperatoroptions"></a>

```json
{
  "operatorName": "string"
}
```

Used to provide a search operator for boolean properties. This is optional. Search operators let users restrict the query to specific fields relevant to the type of item being searched.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|operatorName|string|false|none|Indicates the operator name required in the query in order to isolate the boolean property. For example, if operatorName is *closed* and the property's name is *isClosed*, then queries like *closed:<value>* show results only where the value of the property named *isClosed* matches *<value>*. By contrast, a search that uses the same *<value>* without an operator returns all items where *<value>* matches the value of any String properties or text within the content field for the item. The operator name can only contain lowercase letters (a-z). The maximum length is 32 characters.|

Contains information regarding an ongoing conference (aka call) for a meeting space.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|abuseReportingConfig|[AbuseReportingConfig](#schemaabusereportingconfig)|false|none|Abuse reporting configuration for the ongoing conference.|
|artifactOwner|[UserDisplayInfo](#schemauserdisplayinfo)|false|none|Output only. Display name of the owner of artifacts generated in this conference. The expected use of this in clients is to present info like "This recording will be sent to John Doe's Drive". This field can be empty if preferred display name determination fails for any reason.|
|attachedDocuments|[[DocumentInfo](#schemadocumentinfo)]|false|read-only|Output only. Documents attached to an ongoing conference.|
|availableAccessTypes|[string]|false|none|List of available access types of the conference.|
|availableReactions|[[ReactionInfo](#schemareactioninfo)]|false|read-only|Output only. The set of reactions that clients are allowed to send and can expect to receive. Note that a device in the conference should have the MAY_SEND_REACTIONS privilege to be able to send reactions.|
|broadcastSessionInfo|[BroadcastSessionInfo](#schemabroadcastsessioninfo)|false|none|Information about active broadcast session in the ongoing conference.|
|calendarEventId|string|false|read-only|Output only. The calendar event ID of a Google Calendar event that the meeting space is associated with. If the meeting space is not associated with an event in Google Calendar, this field is empty. For recurring events, it refers to the recurring instance associated with the current call, as determined by the server.|
|coActivity|[CoActivity](#schemacoactivity)|false|none|The current co-activity session, or unset if there is none in progress. A co-activity session can be initiated by devices in JOINED state . Initiator of the co-activity is expected to populate this field to start the session. Once clients detect that the co-activity has finished, any JOINED device can clear this field to end the co-activity session. In the case of switching activities, the initiator of the new activity merely needs to override this with the new co-activity data, and all connected clients are expected to handle the transition gracefully.|
|collaboration|[Collaboration](#schemacollaboration)|false|none|The current collaboration session, or unset if no collaboration is in progress.|
|cseInfo|[CseInfo](#schemacseinfo)|false|none|CSE information for the ongoing conference.|
|maxJoinedDevices|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Output only. The maximum number of devices that may be in the joined state simultaneously in this conference. This can be used by clients to guess whether it will be possible to join, but the only way to know is to try to join. It can also be used to inform users about the limit that is in effect. This limit is normally set when the conference is created and not changed during the lifetime of the conference. But there are some cases where it may change, so clients should be aware that the information may be stale.|
|organizationName|string|false|read-only|Output only. The name or description of the organization or domain that the organizer belongs to. The expected use of this in clients is to present messages like "John Doe (outside of Google.com) is trying to join this call", where "Google.com" is the organization name. The field will be empty if the organization name could not be determined, possibly because of a backend error.|
|paygateInfo|[PaygateInfo](#schemapaygateinfo)|false|none|Paygate information to clients.|
|presenter|[Presenter](#schemapresenter)|false|none|The current presenter in the call, or unset if there is no current presenter. Clients can set this to change the presenter.|
|recordingInfo|[RecordingInfo](#schemarecordinginfo)|false|none|Deprecated, use RecordingSessionInfo instead. Info about recording for this conference. This will always be set in server responses, with a valid recording status. This is superseded by streaming_sessions field, which contains the same information about this recording as well as additional information about other application type at the same time. This will be deprecated and removed at some point.|
|recordingSessionInfo|[RecordingSessionInfo](#schemarecordingsessioninfo)|false|none|Information about active recording session in the ongoing conference.|
|settings|[CallSettings](#schemacallsettings)|false|none|Settings of the ongoing conference.|
|streamingSessions|[[StreamingSessionInfo](#schemastreamingsessioninfo)]|false|read-only|Output only. Info about streaming sessions (recording or broadcast) for this conference. This should contain all active sessions. Currently, it's guaranteed to have at most one recording and at most one broadcast (at most two sessions in total). For each application type (recording or broadcast), latest inactive session is included if there's no active one.|
|transcriptionSessionInfo|[TranscriptionSessionInfo](#schematranscriptionsessioninfo)|false|none|Information about active transcription session in the ongoing conference.|
|viewerCount|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of devices viewing the conference - MeetingDevices that are in VIEWER role and JOINED state in the conference.|
|youTubeBroadcastSessionInfos|[[YouTubeBroadcastSessionInfo](#schemayoutubebroadcastsessioninfo)]|false|none|Information about active YouTube broadcast sessions in the ongoing conference.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|availableAccessTypes|ACCESS_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|availableAccessTypes|ACCESS_TYPE_OPEN|
|availableAccessTypes|ACCESS_TYPE_TRUSTED|
|availableAccessTypes|ACCESS_TYPE_RESTRICTED|
|availableAccessTypes|ACCESS_TYPE_CLOSED|

<h2 id="tocS_CapTokenHolderProto">CapTokenHolderProto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacaptokenholderproto"></a>
<a id="schema_CapTokenHolderProto"></a>
<a id="tocScaptokenholderproto"></a>
<a id="tocscaptokenholderproto"></a>

```json
{
  "tokenHmacSha1Prefix": "string"
}
```

Represents a principal which possesses a particular secret string whose cryptographic hash is specified here. CapTokens ("Capability Tokens") are used in ACLProto. It's expected that ACLs with CapTokenHolders will strongly enforce them by Keystore-wrapping crypto keys for the corresponding CapTokens.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenHmacSha1Prefix|string(byte)|false|none|The hash of the corresponding capability token. The value is defined to be identical to the one in acl.proto's CapTokenMetadata: 10-byte prefix of HMAC-SHA1 of the token. The HMAC key is the following fixed (non-secret) 512-bit value: 79b1c8f4 82baf523 b8a9ab4a e960f438 c45be041 11f1f222 e8a3f64d aeb05e3d c3576acc ec649194 aede422c 4e48e0d1 ff21234a a6ed6b49 a7fa592e efd7bba3|

<h2 id="tocS_CircleProto">CircleProto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacircleproto"></a>
<a id="schema_CircleProto"></a>
<a id="tocScircleproto"></a>
<a id="tocscircleproto"></a>

```json
{
  "circleId": "string",
  "ownerGaiaId": "string",
  "requiredConsistencyTimestampUsec": "string"
}
```

Represents a Google+ Circle. Currently (12/2011), a Circle is identical to the ContactGroup with matching parameters, but Circle must only be used for true Circles and not other Focus groups, and should be preferred over ContactGroup where applicable. Soon it may become more efficient to check membership in a Circle than in a ContactGroup (see http://go/superglue). Support for this principal type is currently (12/2011) incomplete -- e.g., Keystore does not support it yet (see b/5703421).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|circleId|string(int64)|false|none|Circle ID is unique only relative to the owner's Gaia ID. Currently required.|
|ownerGaiaId|string(int64)|false|none|The owner of the circle. Currently required.|
|requiredConsistencyTimestampUsec|string(int64)|false|none|If present, then tests for membership in this circle must use data known to be at least as fresh as the given (FBS-assigned) timestamp. See http://go/fbs-consistent-read-after-important-write Before using this, be sure that any service checking authorization against this circle supports checking consistency timestamps. For example, as of 12/2011, Keystore only supports this for the Moonshine configuration, and in others authorization checks will fail if the timestamp is present.|

|sessionContext|[SessionContext](#schemasessioncontext)|false|none|Contains information about the session which created this history record. This will be empty if the history record was generated by an internal request.|

```json
}
```

ClusterInfo contains clustering related information for a particular thread that would be sent as part of the conversation view. Today, this information would be used by iOS notification server to identify whether the thread belongs to a cluster. If the thread belongs to a grouped cluster, it would identify whether the cluster is throttled.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|[string]|false|none|IDs of the highest priority clusters to which the thread belongs to. If this field is not present, the thread does not belong to any cluster and would be shown in the inbox, unclustered.|
|throttled|boolean|false|none|If the thread belongs to a grouped cluster and all of those clusters are throttled, then this field is set to true.|

<h2 id="tocS_Color">Color</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacolor"></a>
<a id="schema_Color"></a>
<a id="tocScolor"></a>
<a id="tocscolor"></a>

```json
{
  "alpha": 0,
  "blue": 0,
  "green": 0,
  "red": 0
}
```

Represents a color in the RGBA color space. This representation is designed for simplicity of conversion to/from color representations in various languages over compactness. For example, the fields of this representation can be trivially provided to the constructor of `java.awt.Color` in Java; it can also be trivially provided to UIColor's `+colorWithRed:green:blue:alpha` method in iOS; and, with just a little work, it can be easily formatted into a CSS `rgba()` string in JavaScript. This reference page doesn't carry information about the absolute color space that should be used to interpret the RGB value (e.g. sRGB, Adobe RGB, DCI-P3, BT.2020, etc.). By default, applications should assume the sRGB color space. When color equality needs to be decided, implementations, unless documented otherwise, treat two colors as equal if all their red, green, blue, and alpha values each differ by at most 1e-5. Example (Java): import com.google.type.Color; // ... public static java.awt.Color fromProto(Color protocolor) { float alpha = protocolor.hasAlpha() ? protocolor.getAlpha().getValue() : 1.0; return new java.awt.Color( protocolor.getRed(), protocolor.getGreen(), protocolor.getBlue(), alpha); } public static Color toProto(java.awt.Color color) { float red = (float) color.getRed(); float green = (float) color.getGreen(); float blue = (float) color.getBlue(); float denominator = 255.0; Color.Builder resultBuilder = Color .newBuilder() .setRed(red / denominator) .setGreen(green / denominator) .setBlue(blue / denominator); int alpha = color.getAlpha(); if (alpha != 255) { result.setAlpha( FloatValue .newBuilder() .setValue(((float) alpha) / denominator) .build()); } return resultBuilder.build(); } // ... Example (iOS / Obj-C): // ... static UIColor* fromProto(Color* protocolor) { float red = [protocolor red]; float green = [protocolor green]; float blue = [protocolor blue]; FloatValue* alpha_wrapper = [protocolor alpha]; float alpha = 1.0; if (alpha_wrapper != nil) { alpha = [alpha_wrapper value]; } return [UIColor colorWithRed:red green:green blue:blue alpha:alpha]; } static Color* toProto(UIColor* color) { CGFloat red, green, blue, alpha; if (![color getRed:&red green:&green blue:&blue alpha:&alpha]) { return nil; } Color* result = [[Color alloc] init]; [result setRed:red]; [result setGreen:green]; [result setBlue:blue]; if (alpha <= 0.9999) { [result setAlpha:floatWrapperWithValue(alpha)]; } [result autorelease]; return result; } // ... Example (JavaScript): // ... var protoToCssColor = function(rgb_color) { var redFrac = rgb_color.red || 0.0; var greenFrac = rgb_color.green || 0.0; var blueFrac = rgb_color.blue || 0.0; var red = Math.floor(redFrac * 255); var green = Math.floor(greenFrac * 255); var blue = Math.floor(blueFrac * 255); if (!('alpha' in rgb_color)) { return rgbToCssColor(red, green, blue); } var alphaFrac = rgb_color.alpha.value || 0.0; var rgbParams = [red, green, blue].join(','); return ['rgba(', rgbParams, ',', alphaFrac, ')'].join(''); }; var rgbToCssColor = function(red, green, blue) { var rgbNumber = new Number((red << 16) | (green << 8) | blue); var hexString = rgbNumber.toString(16); var missingZeros = 6 - hexString.length; var resultBuilder = ['#']; for (var i = 0; i < missingZeros; i++) { resultBuilder.push('0'); } resultBuilder.push(hexString); return resultBuilder.join(''); }; // ...

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alpha|number(float)|false|none|The fraction of this color that should be applied to the pixel. That is, the final pixel color is defined by the equation: `pixel color = alpha * (this color) + (1.0 - alpha) * (background color)` This means that a value of 1.0 corresponds to a solid color, whereas a value of 0.0 corresponds to a completely transparent color. This uses a wrapper message rather than a simple float scalar so that it is possible to distinguish between a default value and the value being unset. If omitted, this color object is rendered as a solid color (as if the alpha value had been explicitly given a value of 1.0).|
|blue|number(float)|false|none|The amount of blue in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|
|green|number(float)|false|none|The amount of green in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|
|red|number(float)|false|none|The amount of red in the color as a value in the interval [0, 1].|

<h2 id="tocS_CommunalLabelTag">CommunalLabelTag</h2>

<a id="schema_CommunalLabelTag"></a>
<a id="tocScommunallabeltag"></a>
<a id="tocscommunallabeltag"></a>

```json
{
  "creatorUserId": "string",
  "labelId": "string"
}
```

An individual instance (or "tag") of a label configured as a communal type that's associated with a message.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|creatorUserId|string(int64)|false|none|Gaia ID of the user who added the tag, if any. Not present for any tags automatically created by server-side processing.|
|labelId|string|false|none|A string ID representing the label. Possible ID values are documented at go/chat-labels-howto:ids. Example: "^*t_p" for "Pinned".|

<h2 id="tocS_ContactGroupProto">ContactGroupProto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontactgroupproto"></a>
<a id="schema_ContactGroupProto"></a>
<a id="tocScontactgroupproto"></a>
<a id="tocscontactgroupproto"></a>

```json
{
  "groupId": "string",
  "ownerGaiaId": "string",
  "requiredConsistencyTimestampUsec": "string"
}
```

A group of contacts for a given user, as described in http://cs/p#google3/focus/backend/proto/backend.proto Historically (and in still-existing ACLs), this was used to represent Google+ circles as well as contact groups, but this use is now deprecated. New code should use the CIRCLE principal type to represent Google+ circles.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|string(int64)|false|none|Group ID is unique only relative to the owner's Gaia ID.|
|ownerGaiaId|string(int64)|false|none|none|
|requiredConsistencyTimestampUsec|string(int64)|false|none|If present, then tests for membership in this ContactGroup must use data known to be at least as fresh as the given (FBS-assigned) timestamp. See http://go/fbs-consistent-read-after-important-write Before using this, be sure that any service checking authorization against this group supports checking consistency timestamps. For example, as of 12/2011, Keystore only supports this for the Moonshine configuration, and in others authorization checks will fail if the timestamp is present.|

<h2 id="tocS_ContextAttribute">ContextAttribute</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontextattribute"></a>
<a id="schema_ContextAttribute"></a>
<a id="tocScontextattribute"></a>
<a id="tocscontextattribute"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "values": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

A named attribute associated with an item which can be used for influencing the ranking of the item based on the context in the request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the attribute. It should not be empty. The maximum length is 32 characters. The name must start with a letter and can only contain letters (A-Z, a-z) or numbers (0-9). The name will be normalized (lower-cased) before being matched.|
|values|[string]|false|none|Text values of the attribute. The maximum number of elements is 10. The maximum length of an element in the array is 32 characters. The value will be normalized (lower-cased) before being matched.|

```json
  "toolbar": {
    "color": "string",
    "iconUrl": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }

```

The markup for developers to specify the contents of a contextual AddOn. A contextual AddOn is triggered in context of an email. For that email, there can be N items that are associated with the email (e.g. contacts, sales lead, meeting information). Each item is represented as a "card". A card has two views, collapsed and detailed. If there are more than 1 card, the cards are show as a list of collapsed views. The end user can expand into the detailed view for each of those cards. In the detailed view, developers have the freedom to use a variety of "widgets" to construct it. The model here is to restrict (make consistent for end users) the navigation of the N cards but providing developers the freedom to build the detailed view that can best represent their use case/content. Go http://go/aoig-widgets1 to see the mocks. Post v1, we plan to support new AddOn use cases that will require different and separate 'templates'. For example, a compose triggered AddOn which will support a new set of use cases with different user interaction patterns. As a result, we will likely need a very different template than this one.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cards|[[Card](#schemacard)]|false|none|A card must contain a header and at least 1 section.|
|toolbar|[Toolbar](#schematoolbar)|false|none|Deprecated.|

<h2 id="tocS_DataSource">DataSource</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocsdatasource"></a>

```json
{
  "disableModifications": true,
  "disableServing": true,
  "displayName": "string",
  "indexingServiceAccounts": [
    "string"
  ],
  "itemsVisibility": [
    {
      "gsuiteDomain": true,
      "gsuiteGroupEmail": "string",
      "gsuiteUserEmail": "string"
    }
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "operationIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "returnThumbnailUrls": true,
  "shortName": "string"
}
```

Datasource is a logical namespace for items to be indexed. All items must belong to a datasource. This is the prerequisite before items can be indexed into Cloud Search.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|disableModifications|boolean|false|none|If true, sets the datasource to read-only mode. In read-only mode, the Indexing API rejects any requests to index or delete items in this source. Enabling read-only mode does not stop the processing of previously accepted data.|
|disableServing|boolean|false|none|Disable serving any search or assist results.|
|displayName|string|false|none|Required. Display name of the datasource The maximum length is 300 characters.|
|indexingServiceAccounts|[string]|false|none|List of service accounts that have indexing access.|
|itemsVisibility|[[GSuitePrincipal](#schemagsuiteprincipal)]|false|none|This field restricts visibility to items at the datasource level. Items within the datasource are restricted to the union of users and groups included in this field. Note that, this does not ensure access to a specific item, as users need to have ACL permissions on the contained items. This ensures a high level access on the entire datasource, and that the individual items are not shared outside this visibility.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the datasource resource. Format: datasources/{source_id}. The name is ignored when creating a datasource.|
|operationIds|[string]|false|none|IDs of the Long Running Operations (LROs) currently running for this schema.|
|returnThumbnailUrls|boolean|false|none|Can a user request to get thumbnail URI for Items indexed in this data source.|
|shortName|string|false|none|A short name or alias for the source. This value will be used to match the 'source' operator. For example, if the short name is *<value>* then queries like *source:<value>* will only return results for this source. The value must be unique across all datasources. The value must only contain alphanumeric characters (a-zA-Z0-9). The value cannot start with 'google' and cannot be one of the following: mail, gmail, docs, drive, groups, sites, calendar, hangouts, gplus, keep, people, teams. Its maximum length is 32 characters.|

<h2 id="tocS_Date">Date</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadate"></a>
<a id="schema_Date"></a>
<a id="tocSdate"></a>
<a id="tocsdate"></a>

```json
{
  "day": 0,
  "month": 0,
  "year": 0
}
```

Represents a whole calendar date, for example a date of birth. The time of day and time zone are either specified elsewhere or are not significant. The date is relative to the [Proleptic Gregorian Calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proleptic_Gregorian_calendar). The date must be a valid calendar date between the year 1 and 9999.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|day|integer(int32)|false|none|Day of month. Must be from 1 to 31 and valid for the year and month.|
|month|integer(int32)|false|none|Month of date. Must be from 1 to 12.|
|year|integer(int32)|false|none|Year of date. Must be from 1 to 9999.|

<h2 id="tocS_DateOperatorOptions">DateOperatorOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadateoperatoroptions"></a>
<a id="schema_DateOperatorOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSdateoperatoroptions"></a>
<a id="tocsdateoperatoroptions"></a>

```json
{
  "greaterThanOperatorName": "string",
  "lessThanOperatorName": "string",
  "operatorName": "string"
}
```

Optional. Provides a search operator for date properties. Search operators let users restrict the query to specific fields relevant to the type of item being searched.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|greaterThanOperatorName|string|false|none|Indicates the operator name required in the query in order to isolate the date property using the greater-than operator. For example, if greaterThanOperatorName is *closedafter* and the property's name is *closeDate*, then queries like *closedafter:<value>* show results only where the value of the property named *closeDate* is later than *<value>*. The operator name can only contain lowercase letters (a-z). The maximum length is 32 characters.|
|lessThanOperatorName|string|false|none|Indicates the operator name required in the query in order to isolate the date property using the less-than operator. For example, if lessThanOperatorName is *closedbefore* and the property's name is *closeDate*, then queries like *closedbefore:<value>* show results only where the value of the property named *closeDate* is earlier than *<value>*. The operator name can only contain lowercase letters (a-z). The maximum length is 32 characters.|
|operatorName|string|false|none|Indicates the actual string required in the query in order to isolate the date property. For example, suppose an issue tracking schema object has a property named *closeDate* that specifies an operator with an operatorName of *closedon*. For searches on that data, queries like *closedon:<value>* show results only where the value of the *closeDate* property matches *<value>*. By contrast, a search that uses the same *<value>* without an operator returns all items where *<value>* matches the value of any String properties or text within the content field for the indexed datasource. The operator name can only contain lowercase letters (a-z). The maximum length is 32 characters.|
